text:
Alex (oncall): :rotating_light: Getting multiple customer escalations — hitting 500s from the API when they should be seeing 429s. Started at ~09:12 UTC. Can SRE triage?

Tara (support): Customers report sudden spike of 500 responses for quota checks across regions. Example call from customer A: they get 500 body 'internal error' when calling /v1/usage/check. They said it started right after a deploy.

Sam (sre): I see elevated 5xx from rateguard/proxy in prod-aws-us-west-2. Errors are concentrated on rateguard->quota-orch calls. Looking at tracer, quota-orch returned 502/504 on a subset, then our gateway returned 500 instead of mapping to 429.

Maya (eng-runtime): Reproduced locally by replaying request headers from customer A. If quota-orch times out (upstream), routing layer falls back to legacy path which returns a 500 JSON: `{"error":"upstream failure"}` — that's wrong; should translate to a client 429 or 503 with clear reason.

Jon (quota-service): We're seeing periodic timeouts to quota-classifier pods — latencies hit 3s then pod reports 504. Post-deploy we changed sidecar env that influences connection pooling (CONN_MAX=200 -> 50). Might be causing connection saturation under burst.

Alex (oncall): Can we confirm timeline: which deploy, which config change? Incident bot, paste last deploy?

deploy-bot: Deploy completed: rateguard v2.4.1 by maya at 2176543165. Rollout percentage: 100%.

Sam (sre): Stack of events we see: 1) rateguard v2.4.1 rolled 2) quota-classifier pods with new sidecar started recycling 3) upstream connection pools dropped -> timeouts to quota-orch 4) rateguard fallback path executed, returning 500 instead of mapping to 429.

Tara (support): Customers want repro steps. Any safe way to reproduce without hitting production?

Maya (eng-runtime): Repro steps (dev cluster):
```
# replay problematic headers
curl -v -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \
  -H "X-RateKey: customer-A" \
  -d '{"req": {"tokens": 5000}}' \
  https://api.dev.redwood/v1/usage/check
```
If you forcibly drop quota-classifier connections (iptables -A OUTPUT -m statistic --mode random --probability 0.6 -j DROP) you'll see quota-orch timeouts and rateguard emitting 500 body.

Jon (quota-service): Quick mitigation: increase sidecar CONN_MAX back to 200 and restart quota-classifier pods on impacted nodes. Also, we need rateguard to map upstream 504/502 into 429 when appropriate — currently there's a fallthrough.

Sam (sre): Rolling a hotfix: pin rateguard routing to pre-v2.4.1 for traffic from tiered customers and flip sidecar config. Performing partial rollback to restore expected behavior.

deploy-bot: Rollout initiated: rateguard rollback -> v2.4.0. Targeted percentage: 50% at 2176543240.

Lee (billing): Notifying accounts with potential billing impact. Which customers hit token miscount? We'll need list of impacted tokens.

Alex (oncall): Collect logs for impacted requests. Tara please compile support tickets and any charge disputes.

Tara (support): On it. I pinged the three customers reporting 500s: they confirmed lower traffic now and will wait for follow-up.

Maya (eng-runtime): Root cause hypothesis: a conservative connection-pool change in the sidecar caused upstream timeouts. Rateguard assumed quota-orch would always respond synchronously and had a fallthrough path that returns generic 500 for unknown upstream errors. That's a product/regression mismatch.

Sam (sre): Current status: rollback to v2.4.0 at 50% reduced 5xx rate by ~70% in the canary. If stable in 10m, ramp to 100% and then we can safe-deploy a patch: 1) map upstream 5xx/504 to 429 when classifier returns quota error code, 2) add circuit-breaker + clearer logging.

Jon (quota-service): Also adding an explicit 4xx translation rule in quota-orch for timeout cases where we still have classifier verdict cached. Will add metrics for fallback-path hits.

Alex (oncall): Customer comms plan: Tara will send initial note: acknowledgement + ETA. Postmortem will include timeline, root cause, and mitigation.

incident-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-0895, sev:high, owner: Sam (sre).

Maya (eng-runtime): Action items assigned:
- Maya: revert sidecar config in staging and create PR with connection pool tests.
- Jon: add translation rule + metric for fallback hits.
- Sam: finish rollback and monitor, create runbook for translating upstream errors.
- Tara: send customer ack and compile impacted token list.

Alex (oncall): Thanks team — keep comments here for updates. We'll follow up with a detailed postmortem template after the incident is closed. :thumbsup:
